text: Subject 101-9001 received a double dose of Study Drug XJ-401 during Visit 3 (Week 8), deviating from the protocol-specified dosing regimen.
Subject 102-9002 was enrolled despite meeting an exclusion criterion related to renal function outside the eligible range, which was not identified during screening.
A protocol-mandated biopsy was performed on Subject 103-9003 before written informed consent was obtained.
The treatment assignment for Subject 104-9004 was inadvertently unblinded to site staff after a randomization system error.

A temperature excursion was recorded in the storage freezer at Site 105. The excursion was not caught before the affected drug was dispensed, and Subject 105-9005 was dosed with the out-of-spec product, subsequently experiencing an adverse reaction consistent with the dosing error.

Site 106 used informed consent form v2.1 for Subject 106-9006 instead of the currently approved v4.0. Review confirmed v4.0 added a new warning about a significant drug interaction that was never discussed with the subject before dosing began.
Visit 3 (Week 8) for Subject 107-9007 was conducted 4 days outside the protocol-specified visit window; no safety assessments were affected.
Subject 108-9008 did not complete the non-critical symptom diary at Visit 4 (Week 12); the omission was noncritical to primary endpoints.
Subject 109-9009 took a dose of Study Drug RN-88 approximately 2 hours later than the scheduled administration time. No further action was taken at the time.
Subject 110-9010's vital signs at Visit 2 (Week 4) were recorded using a backup manual cuff rather than the automated device, per site procedure.
A lab sample for an exploratory, non-primary biomarker was collected 3 days outside the specified window for Subject 111-9011. No primary or safety endpoint data was affected.
Subject 112-9012 was given verbal rather than written dietary instructions ahead of a Screening Visit, with no effect on assessment validity.
An IVRS system outage at Site 113 resulted in Subject 113-9013 being dispensed an incorrect study kit assignment.
The ePRO device used by Subject 114-9014 malfunctioned during Visit 3 (Week 8), resulting in loss of patient-reported outcome data for that visit.
Calibration of lab equipment used for sample analysis at Site 115 lapsed past its scheduled service date, discovered during a routine equipment maintenance audit.
An EDC system outage at Site 116 prevented timely entry of Subject 116-9016's visit data within the protocol-specified window.

A temperature excursion was recorded in the storage freezer at Site 117. The excursion was caught by the automated alarm before any dose was dispensed, and the affected stock was immediately quarantined; no subject received out-of-spec product.
A software update to the randomization system at Site 118 caused a kit-assignment list mismatch, discovered during routine reconciliation before any subject was dosed from the mismatched list.
The delegation of authority log at Site 119 was not updated to reflect Dr. Nguyen's role prior to Dr. Nguyen performing Visit 2 (Week 4) procedures for Subject 119-9019.
The continuing review submission to the IRB of record for Site 120 was submitted 12 days after the required deadline.
A source document for Subject 121-9021's Visit 3 (Week 8) at Site 121 was missing the investigator's signature and date at the time of monitoring review.
A staff member at Site 122 signed the quality-of-life questionnaire on behalf of Subject 122-9022 without documenting the reason for the exception.

Site 123 used informed consent form v2.1 for Subject 123-9023 instead of the currently approved v4.0. Review confirmed v4.0 contained only formatting and administrative changes, with no new safety information, and the subject's consent otherwise remained valid.

A routine monitoring visit log for Site 124 was not co-signed by the required second reviewer within the specified timeframe, though the visit itself was conducted correctly and the log's content was accurate.
During a routine monitoring visit at Site 125, it was discovered that a protocol deviation involving Subject 125-9025's Visit 2 (Week 4) from 2024-03-15 was never logged or reported.
An audit at Site 126 found that Subject 126-9026 had received an off-protocol dose that was never submitted as a deviation report at the time it occurred.
During database lock review, the sponsor identified that a missed Visit 4 (Week 12) for Subject 127-9027 at Site 127 had not been documented as a protocol deviation.
A site staff member at Site 128 mentioned during a call that a deviation had occurred for Subject 128-9028, but no deviation report or CAPA was ever filed.

An audit at Site 129 discovered that Subject 129-9029 received a double dose of Study Drug XJ-401 approximately three months earlier; the dosing error itself was never entered into the site's deviation log or reported to the sponsor at the time it occurred.

During a for-cause audit at Site 130, it was discovered that a non-critical lab sample collection window deviation for Subject 130-9030 was never logged in the site's deviation tracking system, despite the deviation itself carrying no safety impact.
